name: Simvastatin
route_note: oral tablet once daily, usually in the evening
owner: generic (many); Zocor brand held by Organon

discovery.note: A semi-synthetic derivative of lovastatin, made by adding a methyl group to the side chain.

tagline: The statin of the landmark 4S and Heart Protection trials
summary: Simvastatin is a semi-synthetic statin derived from lovastatin. Its 1994 Scandinavian Simvastatin Survival Study was the first to show that lowering cholesterol reduces total mortality in coronary heart disease, and it remains a widely used generic statin.
mechanism: Simvastatin is an inactive lactone prodrug hydrolysed in the liver to its open-acid form, which competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase.

Falling intracellular cholesterol activates SREBP-2, which increases expression of LDL receptors on hepatocytes. More receptors clear more LDL particles from the blood, lowering LDL cholesterol; statins also modestly lower triglycerides and raise HDL.
uses: Reduction of cardiovascular events and mortality in people at high risk

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Zocor.

history.title: 4S trial
history.detail: Simvastatin reduces total mortality by 30% in patients with coronary heart disease.

history.title: Heart Protection Study
history.detail: Benefit is shown across a wide range of high-risk patients regardless of baseline cholesterol.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic simvastatin becomes available in the US.

history.title: 80 mg restriction
history.detail: The FDA restricts the 80 mg dose because of increased myopathy risk, based partly on the SEARCH trial.

history.title: Organon
history.detail: Zocor transfers to Organon when it is spun off from Merck.

pk.metabolism: Extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism by CYP3A4

facts: It is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin and itraconazole.
The SLCO1B1 c.521T>C variant markedly increases myopathy risk at high doses.

references.title: Scandinavian Simvastatin Survival Study Group. Randomised trial of cholesterol lowering in 4444 patients with coronary heart disease (4S). Lancet 1994
